Medium: the first JSON object is treated as the analysis
_extract_embedded_json returns the first dict that raw_decode accepts. _results_to_findings only emits the infrastructure finding when that dict has an error key. A decoded object with no readiness_analysis still falls through to an empty findings list.

A model that restates the tool and then gives the analysis produces that shape:


The tool is {"name": "demo_tool", "description": "does a thing"}
{"readiness_analysis": {"actionable_errors": {"is_actionable": false, ...}}}
The first object parses. It has no error key and no readiness section, so the real analysis is dropped and the tool looks clean. That is the same outcome this PR is trying to remove. Without the extractor, this text would fail json.loads and the new error path would surface a READINESS-LLM infrastructure finding.

Keep a decoded object only when it contains readiness_analysis. If every object fails that check, use the infrastructure finding. The new tests cover one JSON object in prose and a response with no JSON. They do not cover an earlier object ahead of the analysis.

Low: any top-level error key discards a real analysis
The schema in readiness_judge_prompt.md has no top-level error field, but the gate is "error" in result. A response that includes both error and readiness_analysis is reported as ValueError during analysis and the readiness findings are dropped. A parse-only sentinel would keep those fields distinct. build_infrastructure_error_finding is called with the default llm context, so this parse failure is classified as final rather than as malformed model output.

## Follow-up Comments
Validate directly decoded responses before returning them.
`288-288`: ** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Validate directly decoded responses before returning them.** If the model returns valid JSON such as `{"error": "I cannot evaluate this tool"}`, `json.loads` succeeds. `_results_to_findings` then defaults the missing `readiness_analysis` to `{}` and returns no findings. Apply the same response-shape check to direct JSON and embedded JSON, and report a missing analysis as a parse infrastructure finding. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cisco-ai-defense/mcp-scanner/825f0d0d0bb99e15be2df292a2c71e703061ffc6/mcpscanner/core/analyzers/readiness/llm_judge.py)) [Open the source location](https://github.com/cisco-ai-defense/mcp-scanner/blob/825f0d0d0bb99e15be2df292a2c71e703061ffc6/mcpscanner/core/analyzers/readiness/llm_judge.py#L288)

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift** **Reject nested objects from incomplete responses.** If the response is truncated after `{"readiness_analysis":{"actionable_errors":{"is_actionable":false}}`, the outer object fails to decode, but its nested object decodes successfully. It has no `readiness_analysis` key, so `_results_to_findings` returns no findings instead of an infrastructure error. Validate the candidate’s response shape and do not accept a nested object from an incomplete response. Based on learnings: validate decoded JSON structure before treating it as a valid object.

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Classify response parsing failures with the parse context.** The builder defaults to `context="llm"`, so this `ValueError` is reported as `final`. The classifier defines malformed response errors as `transient` in the parse context. Pass `context="parse"` so the finding gives consumers the correct retry classification.
